title: Statics
description: This syllabus is designed for a one-semester Statics course after calculus and introductory physics. It emphasizes diagramming, vector reasoning, equilibrium equations, and practical engineering judgment before moving into structural idealizations and energy methods.

resources.title: Engineering Mechanics: Statics (Hibbeler)
resources.description: Standard statics text for force systems, equilibrium, trusses, frames, friction, and virtual work.

resources.title: Vector Mechanics for Engineers: Statics
resources.description: Beer, Johnston, Mazurek, and Cornwell. Strong vector mechanics approach with many engineering examples.

resources.title: Engineering Mechanics: Statics (Meriam and Kraige)
resources.description: Classic rigorous treatment of statics and problem solving.

resources.title: Statics and Mechanics of Materials
resources.description: Integrated bridge from statics into stress, strain, beams, and mechanics of materials.

resources.title: Engineering Statics: Open and Interactive
resources.description: Free interactive statics text with examples, diagrams, and practice problems.

resources.title: Statics and Strength of Materials for Architecture and Building Construction
resources.description: Onouye and Kane. Useful structural-design context for load paths and equilibrium.

resources.title: Engineering LibreTexts: Statics
resources.description: Open engineering mechanics material with worked explanations and conceptual support.

resources.title: MIT OCW Mechanics and Materials I
resources.description: University course material connecting equilibrium and mechanics foundations.

resources.title: Mechanics Map
resources.description: Visual open mechanics reference for statics, dynamics, and mechanics of materials.

resources.title: eFunda Engineering Fundamentals
resources.description: Formula and concept reference for mechanics review.

resources.title: ASCE Structural Engineering Institute
resources.description: Professional structural context for equilibrium, load paths, and structural behavior.

resources.title: Jeff Hanson
resources.description: Excellent statics walkthroughs with many solved problems.

resources.title: StructureFree
resources.description: Engineering mechanics lessons for FBDs, trusses, beams, stress, and strain.

resources.title: The Efficient Engineer
resources.description: Clear visual explanations of mechanics, structural behavior, and engineering analysis.

resources.title: CPPMechEngTutorials
resources.description: Worked examples across statics, dynamics, thermodynamics, and engineering mechanics.

resources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare
resources.description: University lecture support for mechanics and structures foundations.

resources.title: Practical Engineering
resources.description: Applied structural and civil engineering context that makes load paths tangible.

topics.title: Course Orientation, Units, Modeling Assumptions, and Problem-Solving Workflow
topics.description: This opening unit frames Statics as the art of replacing real objects with useful mechanical models. Students learn the habits that keep equilibrium problems organized, checkable, and physically meaningful.

children.title: What Statics Studies
children.description: Students learn what it means for particles and rigid bodies to be in equilibrium and why this course is foundational for engineering design.

children.title: Connections to mechanics of materials, structures, dynamics, and design
Units, Dimensions, and Significant Figures
children.description: Consistent units are part of engineering reasoning, not just formatting. They catch mistakes and preserve physical meaning.

children.title: Force, mass, length, time, and moment units
Modeling and Solution Workflow
children.description: A repeatable workflow helps students move from a messy word problem to equations that match the physical system.

children.title: Read, sketch, define system, draw FBD, choose axes
Write equilibrium equations before substituting numbers
Check signs, units, constraints, and limiting cases

topics.title: Force Vectors and Coordinate Systems
topics.description: Statics begins with representing forces as vectors. This unit gives students the mathematical language for magnitude, direction, components, and resultants in two and three dimensions.

children.title: Vector Representation of Forces
children.description: Students learn to describe a force by magnitude, direction, line of action, and point of application.

children.title: Line of action and transmissibility for rigid bodies
Components and Unit Vectors
children.description: Component form turns geometry into algebra so multiple forces can be added and balanced.

children.title: Unit vector notation along lines and cables
Resultants of Concurrent Forces
children.description: Resultants simplify multiple forces into one equivalent vector for analysis.

topics.title: Particles in Equilibrium
topics.description: Particle equilibrium strips mechanics down to its essentials: forces meeting at a point must balance. This unit builds confidence with force balances before students analyze full rigid bodies.

children.title: Particle Free-Body Diagrams
children.description: Students practice isolating a point-like object and showing every external force acting on it.

children.title: Cables, springs, weights, and contact forces
Two-Dimensional Particle Equilibrium
children.description: This subtopic turns diagrams into force equations in x and y directions.

children.title: Sum of forces in x and y
Three-Dimensional Particle Equilibrium
children.description: 3D particle problems prepare students for cables, spatial supports, and real engineering geometry.

children.title: Sum of forces in x, y, and z

topics.title: Moments, Couples, and Moment Resultants
topics.description: Moments explain rotational tendency and are central to analyzing beams, supports, machines, and structures. This unit teaches students to compute and interpret moments in scalar and vector form.

children.title: Moment of a Force in 2D
children.description: Students learn how a force creates rotation about a point and how distance from the line of action matters.

children.title: Vector Moments in 3D
children.description: Cross products make moments usable in spatial problems with arbitrary geometry.

children.title: Moment about a point and moment about an axis
Couples and Moment Resultants
children.description: Couples are pure rotational effects that can be moved on a rigid body without changing external equilibrium.

topics.title: Rigid-Body Free-Body Diagrams
topics.description: Free-body diagrams are the core professional habit of Statics. This unit teaches students to isolate bodies, represent supports correctly, and convert physical constraints into forces and moments.

children.title: External Forces and System Boundaries
children.description: Students learn that the choice of system determines which forces are external and which interactions disappear.

children.title: Applied loads, weights, contact forces, and reactions
Support and Connection Models
children.description: Students learn the standard idealizations used for pins, rollers, fixed supports, smooth contacts, links, and cables.

children.title: Roller, pin, fixed, collar, ball-and-socket, and journal bearings
Diagram Quality and Error Checking
children.description: A good FBD is a reasoning tool. Students learn how to spot missing forces, double-counting, and impossible assumptions.

children.title: Action-reaction pairs and support count checks

topics.title: Rigid-Body Equilibrium in Two Dimensions
topics.description: This unit applies force and moment balance to planar bodies. Students analyze beams, brackets, ladders, plates, and simple structures using three independent equilibrium equations.

children.title: Planar Equilibrium Equations
children.description: Students learn how translational and rotational equilibrium constrain a body in 2D.

children.title: Sum of forces in x and y
Sum of moments about a chosen point
Support Reactions for Planar Bodies
children.description: Support reactions connect FBDs to actual load transfer through pins, rollers, fixed supports, and contacts.

children.title: Simply supported, cantilevered, and overhanging bodies
Solving for reaction forces and moments
Choosing moment centers to reduce algebra
Determinacy and Stability
children.description: Students learn when equilibrium equations are enough and when a model is unstable or statically indeterminate.

topics.title: Rigid-Body Equilibrium in Three Dimensions
topics.description: Three-dimensional equilibrium prepares students for real supports, spatial frames, machine components, and aerospace structures where forces and moments act in all directions.

children.title: Spatial Free-Body Diagrams
children.description: Students learn to represent 3D supports and applied loads clearly enough to write six equilibrium equations.

children.title: Support reactions for ball-and-socket, bearings, collars, and fixed supports
Vector labels for forces and moments
Six Equilibrium Equations
children.description: A rigid body in 3D requires balancing forces and moments about three axes.

children.title: Sum of forces in x, y, and z
Sum of moments about x, y, and z
3D Engineering Applications
children.description: Students practice spatial reasoning in settings that resemble brackets, shafts, cranes, and aircraft components.

topics.title: Equivalent Force Systems and Distributed Loads
topics.description: Engineers often replace complicated load patterns with simpler equivalent forces and moments. This unit teaches how to preserve external effects while simplifying analysis.

children.title: Equivalent Force-Couple Systems
children.description: Students learn to move forces to convenient points by adding the correct couple moment.

children.title: Reduction of a general force system
Distributed Loads on Beams and Surfaces
children.description: Distributed loads model weight, pressure, wind, and contact loads more realistically than point forces.

children.title: Uniform, triangular, trapezoidal, and function-defined loads
Area under load diagram as resultant magnitude
Centroid of load area as resultant location
Load Paths and Structural Interpretation
children.description: Students connect mathematical resultants to how loads travel through members and supports.

children.title: Gravity, wind, and applied load paths
When a simplification is reasonable or risky

topics.title: Trusses: Method of Joints and Method of Sections
topics.description: Trusses introduce structural systems made of connected two-force members. Students learn how equilibrium reveals member tension, compression, and zero-force behavior.

children.title: Truss Assumptions and Classification
children.description: Students learn the idealizations that make truss analysis possible and when those idealizations apply.

children.title: Method of Joints
children.description: Joint equilibrium solves member forces by treating each joint as a particle.

children.title: Method of Sections
children.description: Sections let students solve selected member forces efficiently without analyzing every joint.

children.title: Strategic cutting through up to three unknown members

topics.title: Frames and Machines
topics.description: Frames and machines contain multi-force members, so they require careful body isolation and interaction forces. This unit deepens students' FBD discipline.

children.title: Multi-Force Member Analysis
children.description: Students distinguish frames and machines from trusses and learn why members must often be isolated individually.

children.title: Whole-system FBD followed by member FBDs
Frames
children.description: Frame analysis focuses on stationary load-supporting assemblies such as brackets and structural linkages.

children.title: Machines
children.description: Machine analysis focuses on assemblies designed to transmit or transform force.

topics.title: Internal Forces, Shear, and Bending Moment Diagrams
topics.description: Internal force diagrams are the bridge from Statics to mechanics of materials. Students learn to reveal axial force, shear, and bending moment inside beams and members.

children.title: Internal Force Resultants
children.description: Students learn what is exposed when a member is cut and why internal forces matter for design.

children.title: Axial force, shear force, bending moment, and torsion
Shear and Moment Diagrams
children.description: Diagrams show how internal shear and bending moment vary along a beam.

children.title: Point loads, distributed loads, and applied couples
Relationships among load, shear, and moment
Engineering Interpretation
children.description: Students learn to connect diagram features to likely stress, deflection, and failure concerns in later courses.

children.title: Maximum shear and maximum moment locations
Preparation for bending stress and beam design

topics.title: Friction and Contact Mechanics
topics.description: Friction makes equilibrium problems more realistic and more conditional. Students learn how contact forces depend on normal force, impending motion, and surface behavior.

children.title: Dry Friction Fundamentals
children.description: Students learn how static and kinetic friction limit or resist motion.

children.title: Coefficient of static and kinetic friction
Friction force direction and limiting friction
Friction Applications
children.description: Students apply friction models to wedges, ladders, belts, screws, and brakes.

children.title: Belt friction and screw friction overview
Contact and Stability Checks
children.description: Friction problems often require checking whether the assumed contact state is physically possible.

topics.title: Centroids, Centers of Gravity, and Moments of Inertia
topics.description: This unit teaches geometric properties that reduce distributed quantities and prepare students for beam bending, torsion, and structural design.

children.title: Centroids and Centers of Gravity
children.description: Students learn to locate representative points for areas, volumes, and weights.

children.title: Centroid of lines, areas, and composite shapes
Center of gravity and center of mass
Area Moments of Inertia
children.description: Area moments of inertia describe how area is distributed relative to an axis and become essential in bending analysis.

children.title: Mass Moments and Radius of Gyration
children.description: Students preview properties that matter in dynamics and rotating bodies.

children.title: Polar moment and product of inertia overview

topics.title: Cables, Virtual Work, and Integrated Statics Applications
topics.description: The final unit consolidates statics reasoning through flexible members, energy-based equilibrium ideas, and cumulative engineering applications.

children.title: Cable Systems
children.description: Students learn how flexible members carry tension and form shapes under concentrated or distributed loads.

children.title: Parabolic cable under uniform load overview
Virtual Work
children.description: Virtual work offers an alternate equilibrium method that is powerful for machines, mechanisms, and systems with constraints.

children.title: Applications to pulleys, linkages, and equilibrium positions
Integrated Design-Style Problems
children.description: Students bring the course together by modeling, solving, and checking realistic engineering systems.

children.title: Combined FBD, equilibrium, friction, and internal-force problems
Load path explanation and result validation
Communication of assumptions, diagrams, equations, and conclusions
